audit.whatIsWrong: TWO SHIPPED FALSEHOODS. (1) content.early says 'his W silence cancels your R later' and spikes[2].text calls Slicing Maelstrom a channel — it is not a channel, so Feral Scream cannot cancel a storm that is already up. A player following that advice holds nothing back, and the Cho'Gath player who holds his silence for the storm wastes it. (2) Vorpal Spikes is called a silence in content.early, whys[2], spikes[2].text and wants.foe[0] — Vorpal Spikes is a SLOW on his attacks; Feral Scream (W) is the silence.
audit.why: Riot's text: Slicing Maelstrom summons a storm that strikes nearby enemy champions — no channel wording anywhere. Vorpal Spikes: his attacks release spikes dealing damage and SLOWING enemies in front of him. Feral Scream: a cone that damages and SILENCES. The mirror audit found and corrected the same falsehood from the Cho'Gath side, so both pages now say the same thing: silence lands on the next cast, not on a storm already running.
audit.corrected: report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns, content.early, content.mid, whys[2], spikes[2].text and wants.foe[0] all corrected. Rupture's 950 range is stated against Kennen's own 950 Q so the spacing advice has a number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Kennen four rows and Skill three in both layers, on a 40.48% matchup, while every whys[N] from level 3 onward says the opposite — 'he out-sustains your poke', 'he owns it', 'you can't blow up a Feast-stacked tank', 'he eats your full combo'. diff read EVEN at 6/10.
audit.why: 40.48% over 210 games is the worst number in this slice. Kennen's window is levels 1-2 before any Feast stack exists; after that a magic-damage poke champion cannot out-damage a stacking health pool, and Feast answers with percent-health true damage. The packet levelChart and the mirror audit agree on Kennen / Skill / Cho'Gath x5.
audit.corrected: All seven rows set in both layers to Kennen / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath with ratings 6/5/3/3/2/2/2, diff TRICKY, diffRating 8.5/10, tone updated, and breakdown.difficulty plus report[14].t brought into line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged zero sequencing cues — there were no cooldown numbers anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Feast 80/70/60, Rupture a flat 6s at 950 range, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 at only 300 range, Vorpal Spikes 8/7/6/5/4. Rupture matching Kennen's own 950 Q range is the fact that decides where he can stand.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt; dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, tradeGood and four phases[N].why now carry real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said 'Build MR for his R' — resistances do not apply to Feast.
audit.why: Feast deals true damage on a percent of health, so armour and MR are the wrong answer to it specifically.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns now say so outright.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are the only sliver of this lane that's yours: a Thundering Shuriken plus Electrical Surge on-hit autos can chip Cho'Gath before he has a single Feast stack to insult your magic damage. But respect his Rupture — if you step in to stack a third Mark of the Storm and he knocks you up, his Vorpal Spikes silence shuts off your follow-up and his W silence cancels your R later. Poke from max Q range, never commit your E-in, and don't trade into the knockup.

edits.before: From level 3 on, this slips away. Cho'Gath out-sustains your poke off Feast and minion HP, and your level 6 R does pitiful chip to a tank instead of bursting a squishy — your single biggest spike is wasted into a HP sponge. Don't burn Flash-R to all-in him; you can't kill through his stacks, and a missed channel hands him a Rupture-silence kill on your fragile body. Use 6 to roam mid or skirmish, not to duel the thing you can't kill.

notes: Highest-severity find in the slice: the Kennen page told the reader Cho'Gath's W silence 'cancels your R later'. Slicing Maelstrom is not a channel — Riot's text says he summons a storm that strikes nearby enemies — so the silence lands on the next cast or not at all. The mirror audit corrected the identical falsehood on the Cho'Gath side, so both directions now agree. Vorpal Spikes was called a silence in four places; it is a slow. The 40.48% win rate had a chart giving Kennen four of seven rows: all seven rows are now flipped in matched pairs onto the packet's chart, and diff / diffRating / tone / breakdown.difficulty / report[14].t were brought into line with it so the page does not rate itself EVEN while every phase says Cho'Gath wins. Packet suspectName 'Land Thundering Shuriken' is a FALSE POSITIVE. Rupture's derived 'grounding' flag is not supported by Riot's description (pop into the air, damage, slow) and was not asserted.
